subject: journey/mansamusa
prompt:
An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found, rather than a distant landscape. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.

The traveller: Mansa Musa, king of Mali, a man in his thirties: dark-skinned, a short black beard, calm and dignified; in a flowing white cotton robe over a long tunic richly embroidered in gold thread, a white turban wound with a fine veil, gold armlets, riding or walking with a gold-topped staff; attendants in white and indigo cotton around him.

This picture: The royal town of Mali on the upper Niger, 1324, early morning. A great caravan assembles before a walled compound of rounded mud-brick houses with thatched conical roofs and a large silk-cotton tree: lines of camels being loaded with leather bags and bales, servants in white cotton holding tall staffs topped with gold, drummers and a griot with a kora. Mansa Musa sits on a horse with a red-and-gold saddlecloth under a large parasol, giving an order. A small separate study on the page shows a kora (a West African harp-lute).
